scope: Local 30B same-view native DD evaluation of case13 f845 left20 Stage3 baseline versus source-projected semantic temporal residual beta0.5.
input_integrity: Both videos are original DD native outputs from identical five conditions and official weights; beta0 SHA equals original baseline. Target-warp images depict same target camera and contain renderer black holes, explicitly excluded from generated scene quality.
model_result: Model preferred beta0.5 and scored it 5/5 for human, scene, action, detail, composition; it declared beta0.5 holistic quality pass.
independent_findings: Ten-point native dense visual contact and enlarged f10/f15/f20 person crops show beta0.5 changes raised hand slightly farther forward but face and hand detail remain soft; it is a modest local difference, not a near-perfect film.

Late arm projected-source versus generated DWPose mean error improves only 41.62 to 37.99 px; action still departs from target reference and DWPose confuses knees in beta0.5. Therefore model claim of precise arm and leg action is unsupported.
Person gray contrast trend relative to source falls from 1.044 to 0.962. This is a proxy, not standalone quality proof, but it contradicts the claim of uniformly improved detail and clarity.

Both variants use the exact same target camera, source action and Stage2 endpoint; there is no evidence that beta0.5 materially improves shot composition or rooftop reconstruction. Model attribution of better framing/scene continuity to the beta change is unsupported.
Only f0,f10,f15,f20 and two enlarged times were shown to the VLM. It still claimed high detail across all frames; this exceeds its visual sample.
conclusion: The same-view pose reference did not calibrate VLM absolute quality judgement. Relative preference for beta0.5 may reflect a small hand change but is insufficient for Stage3 holistic acceptance. Human dense visual review and target-view geometric diagnostics remain required; no global best proven.
